note: Reusable glossary for www.planewx.ai/learn/aviation-weather pages. Definitions are plain-language restatements; source_quote is a verbatim excerpt from the Tier 1 source that backs each definition (checked by src/verify_glossary.py). Links use #page=N for PDFs (PDF page number) or the AIM paragraph anchor. No em dashes.

aim71.title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)

mdllamp.title: Localized Aviation MOS Program (LAMP), NOAA/NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory

mdlmos.title: Model Output Statistics (MOS), NOAA/NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory

mdlnbm.title: National Blend of Models (NBM), NOAA/NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory

n811.title: NWS Instruction 10-811, En Route Forecasts and Advisories (September 2, 2025)

terms.definition: A coded forecast of the weather expected within 5 statute miles of the center of an airport’s runway complex for a set time period.
terms.source_quote: A TAF is a concise statement of the expected meteorological conditions significant to aviation for a specified time period within 5 SM of the center of the airport’s runway complex (terminal).

terms.definition: The standard coded report of the surface weather actually observed at an airport.
terms.source_quote: The METAR and SPECI are the code form used for aviation surface observations (reports)

terms.definition: An unscheduled weather report issued between hourly METARs when conditions change significantly.
terms.source_quote: A SPECI is an unscheduled report taken when any of the criteria given in Table 24-2 are observed during the period between hourly reports.

terms.definition: NWS computer-generated statistical forecast guidance, updated hourly for over 2,000 locations, that refreshes MOS with the latest observations.
terms.source_quote: LAMP is designed to frequently update the central MOS product suite primarily by incorporating the most recent observational data.

terms.definition: A statistical technique that improves computer weather model forecasts by relating model output to observed weather; the NWS uses it to make point forecast guidance.
terms.source_title: Model Output Statistics (MOS), NOAA/NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory
terms.source_quote: Model Output Statistics (MOS) is a type of statistical post-processing, a class of techniques used to improve numerical weather models' ability to forecast by relating model outputs to observational or additional model data.

terms.definition: NWS forecast guidance built by blending many NWS and non-NWS computer models into one calibrated set of forecasts.
terms.source_title: National Blend of Models (NBM), NOAA/NWS Meteorological Development Laboratory
terms.source_quote: The National Blend of Models (NBM) is a nationally consistent and skillful suite of calibrated forecast guidance based on a blend of both NWS and non-NWS numerical weather prediction model data and post-processed model guidance.

terms.definition: Marks a rapid change to a new set of prevailing conditions starting at the stated day and time; everything before it is replaced.
terms.source_quote: The FM change indicator group (FMYYGGgg) is used to indicate when prevailing conditions are expected to change significantly over a period of less than one hour.

terms.definition: Temporary fluctuations with a better than 50% chance, each lasting one hour or less and covering less than half of the stated period; a TEMPO group never exceeds four hours.
terms.source_quote: Last for one hour or less in each instance; and

terms.definition: A 30% chance of a thunderstorm or precipitation event, with its related wind, visibility, and clouds, during a period of six hours or less. It is the only PROB group in NWS TAFs.
terms.source_quote: PROB30 is the only PROB group used in NWS TAFs.

terms.definition: A 40% chance group that NWS TAFs do not use, but U.S. military and international TAFs may.
terms.source_quote: The U.S. military and international TAFs may use the PROB40 (40 percent chance) group as well.

terms.definition: A gradual change expected sometime between the two stated times. NWS TAFs do not use it; some joint civil/military, military, and international TAFs do.
terms.source_quote: International Terminology and Forecast Groups Not Used in NWS TAFs

terms.definition: Low-level wind shear (not from thunderstorms) from the surface up to the stated height, with the wind at the top of that layer, for example WS020/27055KT.
terms.source_quote: Height of the top of the WS layer in hundreds of feet AGL.

terms.definition: A change in wind speed or direction close to the ground; the TAF WS group covers non-convective wind shear from the surface up to 2,000 ft AGL.
terms.source_quote: Forecasts of LLWS in the TAF refer only to non-convective LLWS from the surface up to and including 2,000-ft AGL.

terms.definition: Used when no single wind direction can be forecast, typically very light winds (1 to 6 knots) or near thunderstorms.
terms.source_quote: Variable wind direction. Wind direction is considered variable when it is impossible to forecast a

terms.definition: The wind speed unit used in TAFs.
terms.source_quote: Knots

terms.definition: Follows the mean wind speed and gives the peak gust, for example 16015G25KT is 15 knots gusting to 25.
terms.source_quote: Wind gust. Defined as rapid fluctuations in wind speed with a variation of 10 kts or more between

terms.definition: Visibility unit in U.S. TAFs.
terms.source_quote: Statute miles

terms.definition: Visibility forecast to be greater than 6 statute miles.
terms.source_quote: Visibility ＞6 SM will be encoded as P6SM.

terms.definition: No clouds forecast (0 oktas). TAFs use SKC; the METAR code CLR is not used in TAFs.
terms.source_quote: When zero (0) oktas is forecast, the cloud group is replaced by SKC.

terms.definition: A METAR code from automated stations meaning no clouds detected below 12,000 feet; it is not used in TAFs.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: In automated METAR reports only, CleaR for “clear below 12,000 feet”

terms.definition: Clouds covering more than 0 up to 2 eighths (oktas) of the sky.
terms.source_quote: Few clouds [greater than zero (0) oktas to two (2) oktas cloud amount]

terms.definition: Clouds covering 3 to 4 eighths (oktas) of the sky.
terms.source_quote: Scattered cloud layer [three (3) to four (4) oktas cloud amount]

terms.definition: Clouds covering 5 to 7 eighths of the sky; the lowest broken layer is the ceiling.
terms.source_quote: Broken cloud layer (5-7 oktas cloud amount).

terms.definition: Clouds covering the whole sky (8 oktas); an overcast layer below any broken layer is the ceiling.
terms.source_quote: Overcast cloud layer [eight (8) oktas cloud amount]

terms.definition: Thunderstorm cloud. It is the only cloud type a TAF includes, added to the cloud layer whenever thunderstorms are forecast, even in the vicinity.
terms.source_quote: The only cloud type included in the TAF is CB.

terms.definition: How far up you can see into a surface-based obscuration such as fog, in hundreds of feet; it counts as the ceiling.
terms.source_quote: The vertical obscuration group is used to forecast, in hundreds of feet AGL, the vertical

terms.definition: The lowest broken or overcast layer, or the vertical visibility into an obscuration. VV008, BKN008, and OVC008 all mean an 800 ft ceiling.
terms.source_quote: VV008, BKN008, or OVC008

terms.definition: Height above the airport surface. TAF cloud heights are in hundreds of feet AGL.
terms.source_quote: hundreds of feet Above Ground Level (AGL)

terms.definition: Used in a TEMPO group to show that significant weather is expected to end.
terms.source_quote: No Significant Weather. An indication that significant weather conditions, as expressed by WMO

terms.definition: In U.S. TAFs, the ring between 5 and 10 statute miles from the center of the runway complex; used only as VCFG, VCSH, or VCTS.
terms.source_quote: vicinity is defined explicitly as a donut-shaped area between 5SM and 10SM from

terms.definition: Letter added to TAF times to show they are in Coordinated Universal Time, not local time.
terms.source_quote: The letter “Z” is appended to the end of the date-time issuance group as an abbreviation for Zulu,

terms.definition: The time standard used for all TAF times, shown with a Z.
terms.source_quote: The times in TAFs are stated in UTC.

terms.definition: TAF AMD marks a TAF the forecaster changed before the next scheduled issuance. It replaces the previous TAF immediately.
terms.source_quote: Whenever an amended TAF (TAF AMD) is issued, it supersedes and cancels the previous TAF.

terms.definition: TAF COR marks a TAF reissued to fix a mistake, such as a typo, an incorrect time, or a formatting error.
terms.source_quote: Corrections can be for typos, incorrect times, formatting errors, etc.

terms.definition: The TAF is valid, but the forecaster will not issue amendments, usually because observations are missing or incomplete.
terms.source_quote: This indicates the forecaster has enough data to issue a TAF but will not

terms.definition: A TAF that is not issued, used only as a last resort when observations have been missing for an extended period and a forecast cannot be built.
terms.source_quote: A NIL TAF should not be issued except in rare situations.

terms.definition: An international shorthand for good visibility, no low clouds, and no significant weather. NWS U.S. domestic TAFs do not use it.
terms.source_quote: Although not used by the NWS in U.S. domestic TAFs, the contraction CAVOK (ceiling and visibility

terms.definition: The U.S. government weather agency that issues weather data, forecasts, and warnings, including TAFs.
terms.source_quote: The NWS provides weather data, forecasts, and warnings for the United States

terms.definition: One of 122 local NWS offices; WFOs write the TAFs for their area.
terms.source_quote: In support of aviation, WFOs issue Terminal Aerodrome Forecasts (TAF)

terms.definition: The NWS center in Kansas City that issues national aviation forecasts such as AIRMETs, SIGMETs, and Convective SIGMETs.
terms.source_quote: The Aviation Weather Center (AWC) in Kansas City, MO, issues a suite of aviation weather forecasts

terms.definition: The U.S. agency that sets the requirements for aviation weather reports and forecasts.
terms.source_quote:
the FAA establishes
all requirements for aviation weather reports and forecasts.

terms.definition: The four-letter airport code at the start of each TAF; U.S. mainland codes begin with K.
terms.source_quote: ICAO location identifiers in the CONUS begin with the letter K.

terms.definition: The automated weather station network that is the nation’s primary source of surface observations.
terms.source_quote:
ASOS serves as the nation’s
primary surface weather observing network.

terms.definition: An automated weather station similar to ASOS that generally reports fewer elements.
terms.source_quote: Generally, AWOS does not report all the elements that ASOS reports

terms.definition: A report of weather a pilot actually encountered in flight, shared to help other pilots and forecasters.
terms.source_quote: Pilots can report any observation, good or bad, to assist other pilots with flight planning and preparation.

terms.definition: A plain-language text product in which NWS forecasters describe the weather for an area and explain what the TAF code cannot hold, such as the reasoning behind the forecast.
terms.source_quote: Provide additional aviation weather-related issues that cannot be encoded into the TAF, such as the

terms.definition: Ceiling greater than 3,000 feet and visibility greater than 5 miles.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: VFR.  Ceiling greater than 3,000 feet and visibility greater than 5 miles; includes sky clear.

terms.definition: Ceiling 1,000 to 3,000 feet and/or visibility 3 to 5 miles.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: MVFR (Marginal VFR).  Ceiling 1,000 to 3,000 feet and/or visibility 3 to 5 miles inclusive.

terms.definition: Ceiling 500 to less than 1,000 feet and/or visibility 1 to less than 3 miles.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: IFR.  Ceiling 500 to less than 1,000 feet and/or visibility 1 to less than 3 miles.

terms.definition: Ceiling below 500 feet and/or visibility below 1 mile.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: LIFR (Low IFR).  Ceiling less than 500 feet and/or visibility less than 1 mile.

terms.definition: A local storm produced by a cumulonimbus cloud and always accompanied by lightning and thunder.
terms.source_quote:
A thunderstorm is a local storm, invariably produced by a cumulonimbus (CB) cloud, and always
accompanied by lightning and thunder

terms.definition: A thunderstorm with moderate rain (add - for light or + for heavy rain).
terms.source_quote: TSRA                  –TSRA      TSRA      +TSRA

terms.definition: Showery rain, coded as the SH (shower) descriptor plus RA (rain); -SHRA is light and +SHRA is heavy.
terms.source_quote: For example, heavy rain shower(s) is coded as +SHRA.

terms.definition: A type of precipitation, which the Handbook defines as water particles, liquid or solid, that fall from the atmosphere and reach the ground.
terms.source_quote:
Precipitation is any form of water particle, whether liquid or solid, that falls from the atmosphere and
reaches the ground. The precipitation types are drizzle (DZ), rain (RA)

terms.definition: Fog that restricts visibility to between 5/8 and 6 statute miles; below 5/8 SM it is coded FG.
terms.source_quote: When forecasting fog-restricted visibility from ⅝-6 SM, the phenomena is coded as BR (mist).

terms.definition: A visible aggregate of tiny water droplets based at the surface that reduces visibility to less than 5/8 statute mile.
terms.source_quote:
Fog is a visible aggregate of minute water droplets that are based at the Earth’s surface, and it reduces
horizontal visibility to less than 5/8 SM (1 km)

terms.definition: Extremely small particles, invisible to the naked eye, suspended in the air in numbers large enough to give it an opalescent look and reduce visibility.
terms.source_quote:
Haze is a suspension in the air of extremely small particles invisible to the naked eye and sufficiently
numerous to give the air an opalescent appearance. It reduces visibility

terms.definition: A minus sign means light and a plus sign means heavy; no sign means moderate. In TAFs the sign refers to the precipitation, not the thunderstorm.
terms.source_quote:
The intensity qualifiers are light (-), moderate (no
qualifier), and heavy (+).

terms.definition: A form or checklist for recording flight hazards and the risk they add up to before you fly.
terms.section: Chapter 3, Using a Flight Risk Assessment Tool (FRAT)
terms.source_quote: The form used to record each hazard is known as a Flight Risk Assessment Tool (FRAT).

terms.definition: Marks a METAR or SPECI produced entirely by automated equipment with no human observer checking it. Augmented reports leave it out.
terms.source_quote: The report modifier AUTO identifies the METAR/SPECI as a fully automated report with no human intervention or oversight.

terms.definition: Remark for an automated station that has a precipitation discriminator, a sensor that can identify the type of precipitation. AO1 means the station has none.
terms.source_quote: automated stations with a precipitation discriminator are identified as AO2

terms.definition: Separates the body of a METAR from its remarks, which add detail such as the station type, storm information, and sea level pressure.
terms.source_quote: Remarks are separated from the body of the report by the contraction RMK.

terms.definition: An instrument-derived value for how far a pilot can see down the runway, reported in feet, for example R17L/2600FT.
terms.source_quote: The RVR is an instrument-derived value representing the horizontal distance a pilot may see down the runway.

terms.definition: Remark giving the pressure reduced to sea level in tenths of a millibar with the leading 9 or 10 dropped, so SLP132 is 1013.2 mb.
terms.source_quote: A sea level pressure of 1,013.2 mb would be coded SLP132.

terms.definition: Coded as A plus four digits in inches of mercury without the decimal point, so A2992 is an altimeter setting of 29.92 inHg.
terms.source_quote: an altimeter setting of 29.92 inHg would be coded as A2992.

terms.definition: The greatest distance that can be seen throughout at least half of the horizon circle, not necessarily in one continuous sector.
terms.source_quote: It is the greatest distance that can be seen throughout at least half of the horizon circle, not necessarily continuous.

terms.definition: The temperature to which air must be cooled, at constant pressure and moisture content, to become saturated.
terms.source_quote: Dewpoint is the temperature to which a given parcel of air must be cooled at constant pressure and constant water vapor content for the air to become fully saturated.

terms.definition: A cloud type that manual METARs append to a cloud layer, as in SCT023TCU for scattered towering cumulus at 2,300 ft AGL.
terms.source_quote: SCT023TCU                         Scattered layer of towering cumulus at 2,300 ft AGL.

terms.definition: An unscheduled warning of en route weather that may affect the safety of aircraft operations, such as severe icing, severe turbulence, widespread dust storms or sandstorms, and volcanic ash.
terms.source_quote: A SIGMET is a concise description of the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified en route weather phenomena that may affect the safety of aircraft operations.

terms.definition: The SIGMET issued for thunderstorms over the contiguous U.S. It implies severe or greater turbulence, severe icing, and low-level wind shear.
terms.source_quote: Convective SIGMETs are issued for the CONUS instead of SIGMETs for thunderstorms.

terms.definition: An en route advisory for weather that may affect aircraft safety at intensities below SIGMET criteria, such as IFR conditions, mountain obscuration, moderate turbulence or icing, and strong surface winds.
terms.source_quote: AIRMETs are intended to inform all pilots, especially VFR pilots and operators of sensitive aircraft, of potentially hazardous weather phenomena.

terms.definition: The graphical form of the AIRMET, issued by the Aviation Weather Center for the contiguous U.S. as snapshots 3 hours apart out to 12 hours.
terms.source_title: NWS Instruction 10-811, En Route Forecasts and Advisories (September 2, 2025)
terms.source_quote: The G-AIRMET, a graphical version of the AIRMET, is issued for the same criteria as AIRMETs but are more temporally and spatially precise.

terms.definition: The AIRMET series for IFR conditions and extensive mountain obscuration.
terms.source_quote: AIRMET Sierra describes IFR conditions and/or extensive mountain obscurations.

terms.definition: The AIRMET series for moderate turbulence, strong sustained surface winds, and non-convective low-level wind shear.
terms.source_quote: AIRMET Tango describes moderate turbulence

terms.definition: The AIRMET series for moderate icing; it also gives freezing level heights.
terms.source_quote: AIRMET Zulu describes moderate icing and provides freezing level heights.

terms.definition: A short-term advisory from a Center Weather Service Unit for weather that meets or approaches AIRMET or SIGMET criteria, valid for up to 2 hours.
terms.source_quote: A CWA is a concise description of the occurrence or expected occurrence of specified weather phenomena that meet or approach in-flight advisory

terms.definition: A unit of NWS meteorologists stationed at an FAA air route traffic control center; it issues CWAs.
terms.source_quote: Center Weather Service Units (CWSU) are units of NWS meteorologists under contract with the FAA that are stationed at, and support, the FAA’s air route traffic control center (ARTCC).

terms.definition: An office that issues SIGMETs and AIRMETs. The U.S. has three: the Aviation Weather Center, the Alaska Aviation Weather Unit, and WFO Honolulu.
terms.source_quote: SIGMETs are issued from MWOs. The United States has three MWOs: the AWC, the AAWU, and the WFO Honolulu.

terms.definition: A pilot weather report that contains no urgent information.
terms.source_quote: Routine (UA) PIREPs are issued after receiving a report from a pilot that does not contain any urgent

terms.definition: A pilot weather report of a hazard such as a tornado, severe or extreme turbulence, severe icing, hail, low-level wind shear, or volcanic ash.
terms.source_quote: Urgent (UUA) PIREPs contain information about:

terms.definition: The altitude reference used in PIREPs unless another is stated. METAR and TAF cloud heights are above ground level instead.
terms.source_quote: All altitude references are mean sea level unless otherwise noted.

terms.definition: Rough, milky, opaque ice formed when small supercooled water droplets freeze instantly on contact.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: Rime ice. Rough, milky, opaque ice formed by the instantaneous freezing of small supercooled water droplets.

terms.definition: Glossy, clear, or translucent ice formed when large supercooled water droplets freeze relatively slowly; also called glaze ice.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: Clear ice. A glossy, clear, or translucent ice formed by the relatively slow freezing of large supercooled water droplets.

terms.definition: Ice showing rime and clear, or glaze, characteristics at the same time.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: Simultaneous appearance or a combination of rime and glaze ice characteristics.

terms.definition: High-level turbulence, normally above 15,000 feet, that is not associated with cumuliform clouds, including thunderstorms.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: High level turbulence (normally above 15,000 feet ASL) not associated with cumuliform cloudiness, including thunderstorms, should be reported as CAT (clear air turbulence)

terms.definition: Slight, rapid, somewhat rhythmic bumpiness without appreciable changes in altitude or attitude; reported as light or moderate chop.
terms.source_title: Aeronautical Information Manual, Chapter 7, Section 1 (effective July 9, 2026, Change 3)
terms.source_quote: Turbulence that causes slight, rapid and somewhat rhythmic bumpiness without appreciable changes in altitude or attitude. Report as Light Chop.

terms.definition: The NWS coded text forecast of wind direction, wind speed, and temperature at set altitudes for listed locations, issued four times a day.
terms.source_quote: FB Wind and Temperature Aloft Forecasts are computer-prepared forecasts of wind direction, wind speed, and temperature at specified times, altitudes, and locations.

terms.definition: Computer weather models. Each one forecasts wind, temperature, and other elements on its own grid and schedule, so their answers differ.
terms.source_quote: Each NWP model (i.e., sometimes referred to as computer models) outputs wind and temperature at multiple levels.

terms.definition: The lowest altitude over a place where the air temperature reaches 0°C. There can be more than one.
terms.source_quote: The freezing level is the lowest altitude in the atmosphere over a given location at which the air temperature reaches 0°C.

terms.definition: An hourly, automated 3D diagnosis of icing probability, severity, and supercooled large drop threat, built from satellite, radar, METARs, PIREPs, and model data.
terms.source_quote: The CIP combines weather satellite, weather radar, METAR, PIREPs and NWS model data to provide an hourly 3D diagnosis of the icing environment.

terms.definition: The automated forecast counterpart of the CIP: icing probability, severity, and supercooled large drop threat out to 18 hours, from computer model output.
terms.source_quote: The FIP provides the same suite of products as the CIP (see Section 25.5), describing the icing environment in the future and being solely NWP model based.

terms.definition: Liquid water drops larger than 50 micrometers, such as freezing drizzle and freezing rain, that stay unfrozen below 0°C and can freeze behind ice protection.
terms.source_quote: SLD is defined as supercooled water droplets larger than 50 micrometers in diameter.

terms.definition: The NWS automated turbulence forecast for clear air and mountain wave turbulence, issued hourly out to 18 hours and scaled to aircraft weight class.
terms.source_quote: The NWS produces a turbulence product that is derived from airborne turbulence observations and NWS model data with no forecaster modifications. This product is GTG.

terms.definition: A near real-time turbulence nowcast for the contiguous U.S., updated every 15 minutes by blending the latest GTG forecast with recent turbulence observations.
terms.source_quote: GTG-N provides a nowcast of the current turbulent state of the atmosphere over the CONUS in near real-time, updating every 15 minutes.

terms.definition: The ICAO standard measure for automated turbulence reports. It describes the atmosphere rather than one aircraft, so it does not depend on aircraft type.
terms.source_quote: EDR is the ICAO standard dimension for automated turbulence reporting.

terms.definition: The system that sends automated weather and turbulence reports from commercial aircraft sensors to the ground.
terms.source_quote: Automated turbulence reporting systems are common on many commercial aircraft using the Aircraft Meteorological Data Relay (AMDAR) system.

terms.expansion: Next Generation Weather Radar, the WSR-88D
terms.definition: The network of 160 NWS, FAA, and military Doppler weather radars whose data feeds the radar images pilots see.
terms.source_quote: WSR-88D, also known as NEXRAD, displays these targets on a variety of products

terms.definition: An FAA Doppler radar near major airports, built mainly to detect hazardous wind shear, that updates as often as once a minute in hazardous weather mode.
terms.source_quote: The terminal Doppler weather radar (TDWR) is a Doppler weather radar system operated by the FAA, which is used primarily for the detection of hazardous wind shear conditions, precipitation, and winds aloft on and near major airports situated in climates with great exposure to thunderstorms

terms.definition: The unit radar uses for reflectivity, the power returned from a target. Higher values generally mean heavier precipitation.
terms.source_quote: This reflective power, commonly referred to by meteorologists as “reflectivity,” is measured in terms of dBZ.

terms.definition: The strongest radar return found anywhere in the vertical column above each point. Avionics NEXRAD mosaics use it.
terms.source_quote: Composite Reflectivity is the maximum echo intensity (reflectivity) detected within a column of the atmosphere above a location.

terms.definition: Radar returns from the lowest scan only, 0.5° above the horizon. It arrives sooner than composite but can miss heavier precipitation higher up.
terms.source_quote: The Base Reflectivity product is a display of both the location and intensity of reflectivity data from the lowest elevation angle scan, or 0.5° above the horizon.

terms.definition: An estimate of the top of the precipitation, from the height of the 18 dBZ radar echo above sea level. Cloud tops are higher.
terms.source_quote: An Echo Tops product provides an estimation of the top of the precipitation by using the height of 18 dBZ radar echo above sea level.

terms.definition: Many single-site radar images stitched into one regional or national picture. Its time stamp is the mosaic’s age, not the weather’s.
terms.source_quote: A radar mosaic consists of multiple single-site radar images combined to produce a radar image on a regional or national scale.

terms.definition: The free FAA broadcast of weather and aeronautical information to ADS-B In receivers over the 978 MHz UAT link.
terms.source_quote: FIS-B over Universal Access Transceiver (UAT) datalink service provides aeronautical information and meteorological information to the flight deck for aircraft operating in the NAS.

terms.definition: How old weather data is by the time you see it, counting collection, processing, transmission, and display.
terms.source_quote: Latency is the element of data age.
